exposure: Complete vitamin C deprivation (from E10 or E20 to E50 of intrauterine life)
cohort: Guinea pig foetuses were completely deprived of vitamin C from the 10th (E2 group) or 20th (E1 group) to the 50th day of intrauterine life.
finding: Complete vitamin C deprivation in guinea pig foetuses caused marked gross changes including cerebral bleeding, porencephaly, and lissencephalic cerebellar surface, as well as microscopic diffuse bleeding, neuron loss, dysplastic cerebellar changes, and decreased expression of specific collagen-related genes.
gest_age: Deprivation and observation occurred from the 10th or 20th day to the 50th day of intrauterine life.
